articles.title: FAQ
articles.description: Common questions.
articles.content:
### The menu does not open

Check that **GD3D11** is installed and active (the menu is drawn by its DirectX 11 renderer) and that **Union** loads the DLL from `system\Autorun`. Press **Insert** in the game, not in Gothic's main menu.

### Does it work with other versions of Gothic?

Only the Steam version with `GothicMod.exe` 1.08k_mod for now.

### Is the trainer in English?

The docs are. The in-game menu is in Polish for now — an English interface is planned.

### Can I use it in multiplayer?

No — single-player only.

### The game crashed

Start the game again — the trainer detects the crash and prepares a draft report in the Tester hub. See [Testing and reporting](doc:testing).

### Something got stuck (dialogue, hero, NPC)

Use the rescue buttons in [Diagnostics](doc:diagnostics).

articles.title: Installation
articles.description: Requirements, install, update and uninstall.
articles.content:
## Requirements

| What | Notes |
|---|---|
| **Gothic 1 from Steam** | with `GothicMod.exe` 1.08k_mod (Player Kit) |
| **[Union](https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2787491081)** | loads DLLs from `system\Autorun` — the trainer does not start without it |
| **[GD3D11](https://github.com/Kirides/GD3D11)** | the menu is drawn by its DirectX 11 renderer — it does not show on the original renderer |

> **Tip:** The easiest way is the **Steam Workshop for Gothic**: subscribe to Union and GD3D11 and start the game through the Workshop launcher.

## Install

### 1. Download

Get `G1CrazyTrainer_buildN.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/dawidseipold/gothic1-crazy-trainer/releases/latest) and unpack it.

### 2. Copy the files

Copy **all files** from the package into `Gothic\system\Autorun`. In Steam: right-click Gothic → *Manage* → *Browse local files*. No `Autorun` folder? Create it in `Gothic\system`.

```text
Gothic\
└─ system\
   └─ Autorun\
      ├─ G1CrazyTrainer.dll
      └─ G1CrazyTrainer_znane.txt
```

### 3. Start the game

Start Gothic as usual (with Union + GD3D11), load a save or start a new game and press **Insert**.

```media
video: From the zip to the open menu in under a minute
```

## Update

Replace `G1CrazyTrainer.dll` and `G1CrazyTrainer_znane.txt` with the new ones. Settings, hotkeys, presets and your report history are kept.

## Uninstall

Delete `G1CrazyTrainer.dll` and every file and folder starting with `G1CrazyTrainer` from `system\Autorun`.

> **Note:** The in-game menu is in Polish for now — an English interface is planned. The docs give the Polish names in brackets where it helps.

articles.title: Introduction
articles.description: What Gothic 1 Crazy Trainer is and where to start.
articles.content:
**Gothic 1 Crazy Trainer** is an in-game trainer and mod menu for the Steam version of Gothic 1. Press **Insert** in the game and you get one menu with everything: your hero's stats and look, cheats, no-clip, free aim, an item and NPC spawner, a party of companions, teleports, ESP and radar, an arena, a zombie apocalypse and a lot more.

```trainer
{"path": "Character › Cheats", "title": "Cheats", "rows": [
 {"t": "toggle", "label": "Immortality", "on": true, "note": "HP does not drop"},
 {"t": "toggle", "label": "Ghost mode", "on": false, "note": "nobody sees or hears you"},
 {"t": "toggle", "label": "Infinite mana", "on": true},
 {"t": "slider", "label": "Damage multiplier", "value": 5, "min": 1, "max": 50, "note": "for the NPC you aim at"}
]}
```

> **Warning:** Single-player only. The trainer is still in testing — back up your saves before you start.

## Where to start

```cards
[
 {"title": "Installation", "description": "Requirements and the 2-minute install.", "href": "doc:installation"},
 {"title": "The menu", "description": "How the menu works, hotkeys and search.", "href": "doc:the-menu"},
 {"title": "Character", "description": "Stats, look, cheats, movement, combat.", "href": "doc:information"},
 {"title": "Testing", "description": "Help test new builds with the Tester hub.", "href": "doc:testing"}
]
```

## What is inside

| Section | What you can do |
|---|---|
| **Character** | stats, skills, look, cheats, no-clip and glide, free aim, aimbot |
| **Inventory** | spawn any item, ready-made kits, automatic pickup and an item map |
| **Characters** | actions on the NPC you look at, a party of companions, everyone around you, NPC spawner |
| **Fun** | arena with waves, zombie apocalypse, polymorph, meteors, spell rain, chaos |
| **World** | time of day, chapters, world speed, teleports |
| **Visuals** | ESP for characters and items, radar, compass, widgets, crosshair, graphics |
| **Tools** | console, compendium of portraits and icons, diagnostics |

## Ideas and help

- Vote for ideas or suggest your own on **[Feedback](/)** and follow the **[Roadmap](/roadmap)**.
- New builds and docs changes are listed in the **[Changelog](/changelog)**.
- Questions go to **[Support](/support)**. Bugs: the in-game Tester hub or [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/dawidseipold/gothic1-crazy-trainer/issues).

articles.title: The menu
articles.description: How the menu is organised, keys, hotkeys, search and presets.
articles.content:
Press **Insert** to open or close the menu. By default the world stops while the menu is open (**Settings › Behaviour › Pause while the menu is open**).

## Keys

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| **Insert** | open / close the menu |
| **Esc** | close the menu, leave no-clip or glide, stop portrait generation |
| **F11** | screenshot (with the menu) — copied to the clipboard and saved to `G1CrazyTrainer_zrzuty` |
| **Shift + F11** | screenshot of a selected area (the image freezes while you select) |
| **Ctrl + F** | search in the current page |

## Layout

The sidebar on the left has the sections (**Character**, **Inventory**, **Characters**, **Fun**, **World**, **Visuals**, **Tools**). Each has a few pages, and every page is made of **cards** with options.

```trainer
{"path": "Character › Movement", "title": "Movement", "rows": [
 {"t": "tabs", "items": ["No-clip", "Glide"], "active": 0},
 {"t": "toggle", "label": "No-clip (flying)", "on": false, "note": "through walls; WASD, Space/Ctrl up/down, Shift x4"},
 {"t": "slider", "label": "Speed", "value": 9, "min": 1, "max": 100, "unit": "m/s"},
 {"t": "toggle", "label": "Enemies ignore you", "on": true}
]}
```

- **Switches** turn an option on and off, **sliders and values** set how strong it is, **buttons** do something once.
- Some cards have **tabs** for modes that cannot be on together (for example *No-clip | Glide*, *Aimbot | Trigger bot*). Turning one on turns the other off.
- Options that need another one say so — e.g. the aimbot needs free aim.

## Hotkeys

Every option can get its own key: click the hotkey field next to the option and press a key or a combination (Ctrl / Alt / Shift + key). Press the same field again to clear it.

## Search

Every page has a search box. It filters cards and options as you type and — if you want — remembers what you typed when you switch pages (**Settings › Remember search**).

## Settings

The gear at the bottom of the sidebar opens **Settings** (*Konfiguracja*), split into tabs:

| Tab | What is there |
|---|---|
| **Menu look** | menu scale, opacity, corner rounding, dimming the game behind the menu, accent colour |
| **Behaviour** | remember search per page, pause while the menu is open, restore the switches that were on last time |
| **Windows and pictures** | a small status window listing everything that is on; make icons of all items |
| **Hotkeys** | every hotkey you set, in one list |
| **Tester mode** | status dots and report flags next to options, the Tester hub — see [Testing](doc:testing) |

```media
screenshot: The menu with the sidebar, a page of cards and the search box
```

articles.title: Appearance
articles.description: Change the head, face, body, skin colour, size and weight of your hero — with a live preview.
articles.content:
> **Note:** In the menu: **Postać › Wygląd** (the in-game menu is in Polish for now).

Change how the Nameless Hero looks. All parts are in one card with a **preview** on a copy of the hero, so you can try things before applying them.

```trainer
{"path": "Character › Appearance", "title": "Look", "rows": [
 {"t": "value", "label": "Head", "value": 2, "min": 0, "max": 10},
 {"t": "value", "label": "Face", "value": 18, "min": 0, "max": 160, "note": "face texture number"},
 {"t": "value", "label": "Body", "value": 0, "min": 0, "max": 3, "note": "body texture"},
 {"t": "value", "label": "Skin colour", "value": 1, "min": 0, "max": 3},
 {"t": "button", "label": "Apply look"}
]}
```

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Head** | head model |
| **Face** | face texture number |
| **Body** | body texture |
| **Skin colour** | skin tone |
| **Scale** | size of the hero — `1` = normal |
| **Weight** | thin to fat — `0` = normal |

The preview updates automatically (or with a button, if you turn auto-preview off). Nothing changes on the hero until you press **Apply look**.

```media
screenshot: The look card with the preview of the hero
```

articles.title: Cheats
articles.description: Immortality, no stagger, ghost mode, damage multiplier and infinite mana.
articles.content:
> **Note:** In the menu: **Postać › Cheaty** (the in-game menu is in Polish for now).

```trainer
{"path": "Character › Cheats", "title": "Cheats", "rows": [
 {"t": "toggle", "label": "Immortality", "on": true, "note": "HP does not drop"},
 {"t": "toggle", "label": "No stagger from hits", "on": false},
 {"t": "toggle", "label": "Ghost mode", "on": false, "note": "nobody sees or hears you"},
 {"t": "toggle", "label": "Ignore drawn weapons", "on": false},
 {"t": "slider", "label": "Damage multiplier", "value": 5, "min": 1, "max": 50},
 {"t": "toggle", "label": "Infinite mana", "on": true}
]}
```

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Immortality** | your HP does not drop. While you control another body ([body swap](doc:target)), it also protects your real hero. |
| **No stagger from hits** | damage goes in normally, but the hero does not react to hits. Together with immortality: no damage and no reaction. |
| **Ghost mode** | nobody sees or hears you — stealing and drawn weapons cause no reaction. |
| **Ignore drawn weapons** | NPCs see you normally, they just do not react to a weapon in your hands. Ghost mode already includes this. |
| **Damage multiplier** | multiplies the damage you deal to the NPC you are aiming at. |
| **Infinite mana** | spells cost nothing. |

> **Note:** *Ghost mode* and *Ignore drawn weapons* are one card with tabs — only one of them can be on.

articles.title: Combat
articles.description: Attack speed, infinite ammo, free aim with an over-the-shoulder camera, aimbot and trigger bot.
articles.content:
> **Note:** In the menu: **Postać › Walka** (the in-game menu is in Polish for now).

## Attack speed and ammo

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Attack speed** | animation speed only while a weapon is drawn — swings, drawing a bow, reloading a crossbow, casting | 1.8× |
| **Infinite ammo** | arrows and bolts refill by themselves while a bow or crossbow is drawn | — |

## Free aim

Aim bows, crossbows and spells yourself. The camera moves **over the right shoulder**, the mouse aims **up and down**, and the shot flies at the character under the crosshair — also above or below you.

```trainer
{"path": "Character › Combat", "title": "Free aim", "rows": [
 {"t": "toggle", "label": "Free aim", "on": true, "note": "bow, crossbow, spells"},
 {"t": "slider", "label": "Mouse up/down sensitivity", "value": 1, "min": 0.2, "max": 4},
 {"t": "slider", "label": "Camera distance", "value": 2.4, "min": 1, "max": 6, "unit": "m"},
 {"t": "slider", "label": "Side offset", "value": 45, "min": -120, "max": 120, "unit": "cm"},
 {"t": "toggle", "label": "Highlight the target under the crosshair", "on": true}
]}
```

```media
video: Shooting a scavenger on a hill with free aim
```

## Aimbot and trigger bot

Both **need free aim** and are tabs of one card — only one can be on.

```trainer
{"path": "Character › Combat", "title": "Aim assist", "rows": [
 {"t": "tabs", "items": ["Aimbot", "Trigger bot"], "active": 0},
 {"t": "toggle", "label": "Aimbot", "on": true, "note": "requires free aim"},
 {"t": "select", "label": "Key", "value": "Mouse side button 4"},
 {"t": "select", "label": "Priority", "value": "Closest to the crosshair"},
 {"t": "slider", "label": "Field of view", "value": 90, "min": 5, "max": 360, "unit": "°"},
 {"t": "slider", "label": "Range", "value": 40, "min": 2, "max": 100, "unit": "m"},
 {"t": "checks", "items": [["Humans", true], ["Monsters", true], ["Party", false], ["Neutral", false]]}
]}
```

### Aimbot

While the key is held, it turns the hero to the target and puts the crosshair on it.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Key** | *Always (with a bow / spell)*, mouse side button 4 or 5, middle button, Caps Lock, V | side button 4 |
| **Delay after pressing** | wait before it locks on | 0 ms |
| **Priority** | closest to the crosshair, closest to you, lowest HP, highest HP | crosshair |
| **Field of view** | degrees around where you look | 90° |
| **Range** | max distance | 40 m |
| **Stick to the target** | do not switch while the target is alive and in range | — |
| **Also hidden targets** | targets behind walls | — |

### Trigger bot

Shoots or casts by itself when an allowed target is under the crosshair.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Reaction time** | delay before the shot | 120 ms |
| **Time between shots** | minimum interval | 450 ms |
| **Attack keys in the game** | *Ctrl + up arrow* or *Left mouse button + W* — as set in your controls | Ctrl + up |

**Targets** are chosen with checkboxes (humans, monsters, party, neutral…), for both modes.

articles.title: Information
articles.description: Name, guild, level, attributes and skills of your hero — and quick buttons to raise them.
articles.content:
> **Note:** In the menu: **Postać › Informacje** (the in-game menu is in Polish for now).

The **Information** page shows your hero at a glance — portrait, name, guild, level, experience, health, mana and all attributes — and lets you change them directly.

```trainer
{"path": "Character › Information", "title": "Progress", "rows": [
 {"t": "value", "label": "Add experience", "value": 1000, "min": 0, "max": 100000, "note": "through the game's own XP function — level-ups work"},
 {"t": "value", "label": "Add learning points", "value": 10, "min": 0, "max": 200},
 {"t": "select", "label": "Guild", "value": "Shadow"},
 {"t": "button", "label": "Max everything"}
]}
```

## Stats

Every attribute (strength, dexterity, max HP, max mana) has a field and a **Set** button. Values are written straight to the hero.

## Progress

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Add experience** | gives XP through the game's own function, so level-ups, learning points and messages work as in the game. Always applies to the character you control. |
| **Add learning points** | adds learning points (LP) to spend at teachers. |
| **Guild** | changes the hero's guild — NPCs react to the new guild right away. |

## Skills

**Max everything** (button in the card header) sets every skill to the maximum, the 6th circle of magic and 100% hit chance in one click.

> **Tip:** Changing the guild changes how camps react to you — set it back if guards suddenly attack.

articles.title: Movement
articles.description: No-clip, glide, hero speed and sprint.
articles.content:
> **Note:** In the menu: **Postać › Ruch** (the in-game menu is in Polish for now).

Two ways to travel without the game's physics — **no-clip** flies through everything, **glide** walks on the ground — plus a speed boost for normal movement. No-clip and glide are tabs of one card: turning one on turns the other off.

## No-clip

Fly freely through walls, rocks and buildings.

```trainer
{"path": "Character › Movement", "title": "No-clip", "rows": [
 {"t": "tabs", "items": ["No-clip", "Glide"], "active": 0},
 {"t": "toggle", "label": "No-clip (flying)", "on": true, "note": "WASD, mouse turns, Space/Ctrl up/down, Shift x4; Esc turns it off"},
 {"t": "slider", "label": "Speed", "value": 9, "min": 1, "max": 100, "unit": "m/s"},
 {"t": "slider", "label": "Q/E turning", "value": 130, "min": 20, "max": 720, "unit": "°/s"},
 {"t": "toggle", "label": "Mouse turns the hero", "on": true},
 {"t": "toggle", "label": "Enemies ignore you", "on": true}
]}
```

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| **W A S D** | move |
| **Space / Ctrl** | up / down |
| **Shift** | 4× faster |
| **Q / E** | turn |
| **Esc** | turn no-clip off — your feet land on the ground |

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Speed** | flying speed (Shift ×4) | 9 m/s |
| **Q/E turning** | how fast Q and E turn | 130 °/s |
| **Mouse turns the hero** | moving the mouse sideways turns, up/down tilts the camera | on |
| **Mouse sensitivity** | for the option above | 1.0 |
| **Enemies ignore you** | monsters and enemies do not notice you while flying | — |

```media
video: Flying through the Old Camp wall with no-clip
```

## Glide

Walk over the ground without physics and animations — fast travel that stays on the terrain.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Glide (on the ground)** | turn it on; WASD, Shift ×4, Esc turns it off | — |
| **Collide with objects** | trees, rocks, bridges, grates, fences — you walk onto them instead of passing through | — |
| **Max slope** | steep walls up to this angle are climbed (90° = any wall) | 50° |
| **Speed / turning / mouse / enemies ignore you** | as in no-clip | 6 m/s |

> **Note:** Object collision on some bridges and grates is still being fixed.

## Speed

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Hero speed** | animation speed of the hero — running, attacks, turning | 1.5× |
| **Sprint** | the running animation of the speed potion | — |

articles.title: Item spawner
articles.description: Find any item in the game and put it in your inventory — weapons, armour, runes, potions, quest items.
articles.content:
> **Note:** In the menu: **Ekwipunek › Spawner** (the in-game menu is in Polish for now).

Every item of the game in one searchable list, sorted into categories (melee weapons, ranged weapons, armour, runes, scrolls, potions, food, plants, keys, amulets and rings, quest items…). Each item shows its icon and price in ore.

```trainer
{"path": "Inventory › Spawner", "title": "Items", "rows": [
 {"t": "tabs", "items": ["All", "Weapons", "Armour", "Magic", "Potions", "Other"], "active": 1},
 {"t": "text", "label": "Ore Baron's sword", "value": "1000 ore"},
 {"t": "value", "label": "Amount", "value": 1, "min": 1, "max": 100},
 {"t": "button", "label": "Add to inventory"}
]}
```

- **Search** by name, filter by category, set the **amount** and add the item.
- **Add ore** gives you nuggets of ore directly.
- Item icons are generated in the game the first time — you can regenerate them in [Compendium](doc:compendium).

```media
screenshot: The item list with icons and categories
```

articles.title: Kits
articles.description: One-click equipment sets for a warrior, archer, mage or thief, and "everything of a kind" buttons.
articles.content:
> **Note:** In the menu: **Ekwipunek › Zestawy** (the in-game menu is in Polish for now).

```trainer
{"path": "Inventory › Kits", "title": "Kits", "rows": [
 {"t": "button", "label": "Warrior"},
 {"t": "button", "label": "Archer"},
 {"t": "button", "label": "Mage"},
 {"t": "button", "label": "Thief"}
]}
```

## Class kits

| Kit | What you get |
|---|---|
| **Warrior** | the strongest one- and two-handed weapon, the best armour, 10 healing potions |
| **Archer** | the best bow and crossbow + 300 arrows and bolts |
| **Mage** | all runes, 20 mana potions, the best mage robe |
| **Thief** | all keys + 30 lockpicks |

## Everything of a kind

| Button | What you get |
|---|---|
| **All runes** | every rune |
| **All scrolls** | every scroll (amount of each is set next to it) |
| **All potions** | every potion (amount of each) |
| **All keys** | every key in the game |
| **All amulets and rings** | every amulet and ring |

articles.title: Pickup
articles.description: Automatic pickup around you, a list of every item lying in the world, and a pickup bot.
articles.content:
> **Note:** In the menu: **Ekwipunek › Zbieranie** (the in-game menu is in Polish for now).

## Auto-pickup

Items on the ground around you go straight to your inventory.

```trainer
{"path": "Inventory › Pickup", "title": "Auto-pickup", "rows": [
 {"t": "toggle", "label": "Pick up automatically", "on": true},
 {"t": "slider", "label": "Range", "value": 5, "min": 1, "max": 30, "unit": "m"},
 {"t": "slider", "label": "How many at once", "value": 5, "min": 1, "max": 50},
 {"t": "slider", "label": "Interval", "value": 0.5, "min": 0.1, "max": 5, "unit": "s"},
 {"t": "checks", "items": [["Weapons", true], ["Potions", true], ["Plants", true], ["Ammo", false]]}
]}
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Range** | how far around you (with the animation at most 3.5 m) | 5 m |
| **How many at once** | items per pass | 5 |
| **Interval** | seconds between passes | 0.5 s |
| **Min. value** | only items worth at least this much ore (0 = everything) | 0 |
| **With the pickup animation** | the hero picks up one item at a time like in the game (slower). Skipped in no-clip and glide. | — |
| **Categories** | checkboxes for what to pick up | all |

## Items on the map

A list of **every item lying in the world** with its distance and coordinates. From the list you can teleport to an item or export the whole list to CSV.

## Pickup bot

Walks (teleports) from item to item along the shortest route and picks everything up. **Esc** stops it. The delay between items is adjustable (default 0.4 s).

```media
video: The pickup bot collecting plants around the Old Camp
```

articles.title: NPC spawner
articles.description: Spawn any character or monster of the game — or move the original to you.
articles.content:
> **Note:** In the menu: **Postacie › Spawner** (the in-game menu is in Polish for now).

Every NPC and monster of the game in a searchable list. Pick one, set how many, and they appear next to you.

```trainer
{"path": "Characters › Spawner", "title": "Spawn", "rows": [
 {"t": "text", "label": "Orc warrior", "value": "monster"},
 {"t": "value", "label": "Amount", "value": 3, "min": 1, "max": 20},
 {"t": "tabs", "items": ["Move the original", "Create a copy"], "active": 0},
 {"t": "button", "label": "Spawn"}
]}
```

- **When the character already exists** — *move the original* (the real NPC with its quests comes to you) or *create a copy*.
- **Spawn by instance name** — type any instance (like the console `insert`) to spawn something that is not on the list.
- **Spawned list** — everything you spawned, with removal; characters from the `insert` command land here too.

> **Tip:** Spawned NPCs can be added to the party right away from the list.

articles.title: Party
articles.description: Companions that follow you, fight for you and do not fall out of the party.
articles.content:
> **Note:** In the menu: **Postacie › Drużyna** (the in-game menu is in Polish for now).

Anyone can join your party — humans and monsters. Party members follow you, fight on your side and can be ordered around.

```trainer
{"path": "Characters › Party", "title": "Party", "rows": [
 {"t": "text", "label": "Thorus", "value": "following"},
 {"t": "text", "label": "Wolf", "value": "following"},
 {"t": "toggle", "label": "Keep the party together", "on": true, "note": "every 3 s: whoever stopped following comes back"},
 {"t": "toggle", "label": "No talking", "on": true},
 {"t": "toggle", "label": "Stop fighting after teleport", "on": true}
]}
```

## Building the party

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Add to party** | on the [Target](doc:target) page, or from the selection list here (radius 30 m) |
| **Everyone around to the party** | everybody within the radius joins and follows you |
| **Disband** | allies go back to their routines |
| **Party list** | each member with portrait and actions: follow, wait (stays exactly where told), teleport to you, remove from the world |

## Keeping them with you

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| **No talking** | party members do not start dialogues with you (that used to pull them out of the party) |
| **Keep the party together** | every 3 s whoever stopped following comes back; whoever is too far (default 30 m) is moved to you |
| **Stop fighting after teleport** | a companion moved to you follows you instead of running back to its enemy |

## Fights

| Option (off = …) | When it is off |
|---|---|
| **Party can fight each other** | party members do not notice or hurt each other |
| **Party monsters attack neutrals** | your wolf bites only enemies |
| **Party humans attack neutrals** | they fight only enemies |
| **Neutrals attack party monsters** | nobody neutral touches your monster |

> **Note:** Fights inside the party are still being tuned — a monster can sometimes stay locked on its last target.

articles.title: Surroundings
articles.description: Everyone around you in one list — with filters and the same actions as for the target.

articles.title: Target
articles.description: Actions on the NPC you are looking at — party, body swap, pull, teleport, kill, revive, rob, spells and more.
articles.content:
> **Note:** In the menu: **Postacie › Cel** (the in-game menu is in Polish for now).

The **target** is the NPC under your view (the game's focus) or one you saved to the list. The card on top shows its portrait, name, guild, HP and what it is doing.

```trainer
{"path": "Characters › Target", "title": "Diego — Shadow", "rows": [
 {"t": "button", "label": "Add to party"},
 {"t": "button", "label": "Body swap"},
 {"t": "button", "label": "Pull to me"},
 {"t": "button", "label": "Revive / heal"}
]}
```

## Saved targets

**Save target** puts the NPC you look at on a list, so you can act on it from anywhere. **Use the NPC in view** goes back to whatever is under your view (the list stays).

## Actions

The buttons change with the state of the target — for example *Add to party* becomes *Remove from party*.

| Action | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Add to party** | the target fights on your side and follows you (mind control) — see [Party](doc:party) |
| **Body swap** | you play as the target; go back with the button in the menu header |
| **Pull to me** / **Teleport to target** | move it to you, or you to it |
| **Launch into the air** | it flies up (height in the action settings, default 15 m) |
| **Kill** | works on immortal NPCs too |
| **Revive / heal** | revives the same character in place — inventory and quests stay |
| **Rob to zero** | the target's whole inventory goes to you |
| **Make a portrait** | a new picture of the target for the list and the [Compendium](doc:compendium) |
| **Freeze / unfreeze** | only this one NPC stands still |
| **Cast selected spells** | random spells from those ticked in the *Magic on target* card, only at this target (damage adjustable, can hit immortal NPCs) |
| **Remove from the world** | the NPC disappears |

> **Warning:** Removing or killing story characters can break quests. Back up your save first.

articles.title: Chaos
articles.description: Launch everyone into the air, freeze the world, Quicksilver mode.
articles.content:
> **Note:** In the menu: **Fun › Chaos** (the in-game menu is in Polish for now).

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Everyone into the air** | NPCs within the radius fly 15 m up | — |
| **Freeze all NPCs** | the world stops, only you move | — |
| **Quicksilver mode** | everything around nearly stops, you move normally (or faster) | — |
| **World speed** (Quicksilver) | `0.05` = almost stopped | 0.12 |
| **Your speed** (Quicksilver) | `1` = normal | 1.3 |
| **Party fast too** | your party moves at your speed | — |

```trainer
{"path": "Fun › Chaos", "title": "Quicksilver", "rows": [
 {"t": "toggle", "label": "Quicksilver mode", "on": true},
 {"t": "slider", "label": "World speed", "value": 0.12, "min": 0.05, "max": 1},
 {"t": "slider", "label": "Your speed", "value": 1.3, "min": 0.5, "max": 3},
 {"t": "toggle", "label": "Party fast too", "on": false}
]}
```

```media
video: Quicksilver mode — arrows hanging in the air
```

articles.title: Combat and arena
articles.description: Arena with waves and rewards, everyone vs everyone, peace, zombie apocalypse and polymorph.
articles.content:
> **Note:** In the menu: **Fun › Walka** (the in-game menu is in Polish for now).

## Arena

Waves of enemies appear 6–10 m around you. They only **knock you down** — being knocked down means you lost.

```trainer
{"path": "Fun › Combat", "title": "Arena", "rows": [
 {"t": "slider", "label": "Arena mode", "value": 3, "min": 1, "max": 20, "note": "starting wave"},
 {"t": "value", "label": "Number of waves", "value": 10, "min": 0, "max": 50, "note": "0 = endless"},
 {"t": "toggle", "label": "Rewards after a wave", "on": true, "note": "ore + 1-2 random items"},
 {"t": "button", "label": "Start"}
]}
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Arena mode** | the starting wave | 1 |
| **Number of waves** | 0 = endless | 0 |
| **Rewards after a wave** | ore and 1–2 random items | on |

Arena enemies are named *Arena: …* so you can tell them apart.

## Factions

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Everyone vs everyone** | every guild is hostile to every other; turning it off makes peace within 60 m |
| **Random guilds** | humans within the radius get a random guild |
| **Peace** | everybody within the radius stops fighting, including with you |
| **Everyone vs you** | while on, everybody within the radius (default 30 m) attacks you; off = peace |
| **Kill enemies in radius** | optionally immortal ones too |

## Zombie apocalypse

The dead rise around you.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Apocalypse** | how many undead rise | — |
| **Spawn distance** | metres from you | 10 m |
| **Health** | HP of each (±25%) | 150 |
| **Protection** | against every damage type | 20 |
| **Can be killed** | off = they are immortal | on |
| **Remove the undead of the apocalypse** | only those created by this option | — |

Story undead are never touched.

## Polymorph

Turns characters within the radius into creatures (and the other way round) — with effects and a choice of targets. At most 30 at once by default.

> **Warning:** Polymorph **removes** the original NPCs — quests that need them can break.

```media
video: An arena wave and the zombie apocalypse around the Old Camp
```

articles.title: Magic
articles.description: Thanos snap, meteors and spell rain.
articles.content:
> **Note:** In the menu: **Fun › Magia** (the in-game menu is in Polish for now).

```trainer
{"path": "Fun › Magic", "title": "Spell rain", "rows": [
 {"t": "toggle", "label": "Spell rain", "on": true, "note": "spells fall on random characters around you"},
 {"t": "slider", "label": "Damage", "value": 80, "min": 1, "max": 1000},
 {"t": "slider", "label": "Every", "value": 0.6, "min": 0.1, "max": 5, "unit": "s"},
 {"t": "slider", "label": "Radius", "value": 30, "min": 5, "max": 100, "unit": "m"},
 {"t": "select", "label": "At whom", "value": "Enemies"}
]}
```

## Thanos snap

NPCs within the radius turn to dust. Choose **who** (everyone, enemies, monsters…), **what share** of them (%), and whether immortal ones count.

## Meteor

A rain of fire on everybody within the radius (damage 150 by default, optionally immortal ones too).

## Spell rain

Spells fall on random characters around you while it is on.

| Option | Default |
|---|---|
| **Damage** | 80 |
| **Every** | 0.6 s |
| **Targets at once** | 1 |
| **Radius** | 30 m |
| **At whom** | filter |
| **Also immortal** | — |

> **Note:** The number of spells in the air is limited to keep the game stable.

articles.title: Teleport
articles.description: Saved places, teleport forward, to your party and to places of the world.
articles.content:
> **Note:** In the menu: **Świat › Teleport** (the in-game menu is in Polish for now).

```trainer
{"path": "World › Teleport", "title": "Places", "rows": [
 {"t": "tabs", "items": ["All", "Camps", "Dungeons", "Mine", "Saved"], "active": 0},
 {"t": "text", "label": "Old Camp — gate", "value": "camp"},
 {"t": "text", "label": "Free Mine", "value": "mine"},
 {"t": "button", "label": "Save current position"}
]}
```

- **Places** — a list of locations with icons by type (camps, dungeons, mines, temples…), filterable with chips.
- **Saved positions** — save where you stand under your own name, rename, delete, teleport back any time.
- **Teleport forward** — jump a few metres ahead and land on the ground.
- **Party** — teleport the party to you, or you to a party member.

> **Tip:** Party members are teleported with you when *Keep the party together* is on ([Party](doc:party)).

articles.title: Time and story
articles.description: World speed, time of day, stopping time and jumping to a chapter.
articles.content:
> **Note:** In the menu: **Świat › Czas i fabuła** (the in-game menu is in Polish for now).

```trainer
{"path": "World › Time and story", "title": "Time", "rows": [
 {"t": "slider", "label": "World speed", "value": 0.3, "min": 0.1, "max": 3, "note": "0.1 = slow-mo, 3 = turbo"},
 {"t": "select", "label": "What slows down", "value": "Characters around"},
 {"t": "toggle", "label": "Party at normal speed", "on": true},
 {"t": "value", "label": "Set the hour", "value": 12, "min": 0, "max": 23},
 {"t": "toggle", "label": "Stop the time of day", "on": false}
]}
```

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| **World speed** | slow motion or turbo — `0.1` to `3` |
| **What slows down** | the whole game or only the characters around you |
| **Party at normal speed** | your party ignores the slow motion (only in *characters around* mode) |
| **Set the hour** | 0–23; your party and spawned characters stay with you |
| **Stop the time of day** | the clock stands still |
| **Jump to a chapter** | runs the game's chapter change |

> **Warning:** Jumping to a chapter runs the same script as the story does — it can break quests of the chapters you skip.

articles.title: Character ESP
articles.description: Boxes, names, health, weapons and lines to characters — through walls.
articles.content:
> **Note:** In the menu: **Wizualia › ESP postaci** (the in-game menu is in Polish for now).

Shows characters through walls, with exactly the details you tick.

```trainer
{"path": "Visuals › Character ESP", "title": "What to show", "rows": [
 {"t": "toggle", "label": "Character ESP", "on": true},
 {"t": "checks", "items": [["Box", true], ["Name", true], ["Health", true], ["Distance", true], ["Skeleton", false], ["Equipment", false], ["Who it attacks", true], ["Type tag", true]]},
 {"t": "slider", "label": "Max range", "value": 50, "min": 5, "max": 200, "unit": "m"},
 {"t": "slider", "label": "Max characters at once", "value": 40, "min": 5, "max": 150},
 {"t": "select", "label": "Box type", "value": "Corners"}
]}
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **What to show** | checkboxes: box, name, health, distance, skeleton, equipment, *who it attacks* (text and arrow to its fight target), type tag ([Arena], [Party], [Spawned]) | — |
| **Show** | filter: everyone, enemies, party… | everyone |
| **Max range** | | 50 m |
| **Max characters at once** | the closest ones; fewer = lighter for slower PCs | 40 |
| **Box type** | 2D box, corners, 3D box | — |

## Arrows and edge markers

- **Arrows around the crosshair** point to characters on a circle (radius 140 px by default).
- **Edge markers** sit on the screen edge where a box left the screen.

Colours are set in [Colours](doc:colours). A **preview** at the top of the page shows the result right away.

articles.title: Diagnostics
articles.description: Screenshots, rescue tools when something gets stuck, and the party test scene.
articles.content:
> **Note:** In the menu: **Narzędzia › Diagnostyka** (the in-game menu is in Polish for now).

## Screenshots

| Option | Key | What it does |

| **Area screenshot** | Shift + F11 | select a rectangle with the mouse (the image freezes; Esc cancels) |

```trainer
]}
```

## Party test scene

Creates a test scene for party fights: Thorus and a wolf in your party, a guard, a bandit, a digger and a molerat as neutrals, a scavenger as an enemy. **Remove the test scene** cleans it up.

articles.title: Testing and reporting
articles.description: Help test new builds with the in-game Tester hub.
articles.content:
Thanks for helping! Everything you need is in the game — in the **Tester hub**. The in-game menu is in Polish for now, so the Polish names are given in *italics*.

## 1. Turn on tester mode

1. In the game press **Insert** → at the bottom of the sidebar open **Settings** (*Konfiguracja*).
2. Turn on **Tester mode** (*Tryb testera*) and click **Open Tester hub** (*Otwórz Centrum testera*).
3. Enter **your nickname** in the top-right corner of the hub — every report is signed with it.

In tester mode every option shows a **dot** — the author's status — and a **flag** that opens a report for that option.

```trainer
{"path": "Any page, tester mode", "title": "Status dots", "rows": [
 {"t": "toggle", "label": "● green — OK", "on": true},
 {"t": "toggle", "label": "● yellow — BUG", "on": false},
 {"t": "toggle", "label": "● red — CRASH", "on": false},
 {"t": "toggle", "label": "● purple — TEST: new, please check", "on": true}
]}
```

## 2. Test

**Checklist** (*Checklista*): for each option click **Works / Partly / Does not work**.

- In alpha builds test mainly **TEST (new)** and **BUG** — use the dot filter.
- Nothing is overwritten: every rating goes to the history with the build number.
- After *Partly* / *Does not work* a form opens — describe what went wrong.

**+ New report** (*+ Nowe zgłoszenie*) — a bug, crash, suggestion or question:

- **What is it about** — the option (searchable list) or "General". Known problems of that option are shown below.
- **Steps** — what you did, in order. The most important field.
- **Attach game state** — world, position, enabled options and recent events, added automatically.
- **Attachments** — screenshot with **F11** / **Shift+F11**, then **Ctrl+V** in the form.

**Crash?** Start the game again — the trainer prepares a draft report by itself.

## 3. Send

**Send** (*Wyślij*) → **Export unsent** creates one file in `G1CrazyTrainer_raporty` (.txt or .zip). **Send it to the author** (Discord / e-mail).

> **Note:** A report contains your nickname, Windows version, CPU/GPU name, RAM, resolution, the list of DLLs in the game folder, trainer settings and its log. Nothing else — it is plain text, read it before sending.

articles.title: Where to post what
articles.description: Ideas, questions, bugs — and what happens next.
articles.content:
**Everything is in English** — ideas, comments and questions — so everyone can follow and help.

| You have… | Where |
|---|---|
| A new feature idea | [Feedback](/) — one idea per post. Search first and vote if it already exists. |
| A question | [Support](/support), or search these docs first. |
| A bug or a crash | the in-game **Tester hub** (best — it attaches everything) or [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/dawidseipold/gothic1-crazy-trainer/issues/new/choose) |

## What happens with an idea

1. **Pending** — new ideas wait for review. Votes help decide.
2. **Approved / Planned** — the idea appears on the [Roadmap](/roadmap) and gets a GitHub issue for the work.
3. **In progress → Needs verification** — it is in a test build and testers confirm it.
4. **Done** — shipped and listed in the [Changelog](/changelog). Voters are notified at every step. Ideas that will not be done are **Rejected** with a reason.

> **Tip:** Ports of open-source Union plugins and mods are welcome **with credit** — link the source in your idea.

articles.title: Component showcase
articles.description: Every element a docs page can use, in one place. Pick what you like; the rest can go.
articles.content:
This page is a test bed. Each section shows one element and how it is written in the markdown files under `docs/pages`.

## Text

Plain paragraphs, **bold**, *italic*, ~~strikethrough~~ and `inline code`. Links to [another docs page](doc:installation), to a [section of a page](doc:installation#requirements) and to [an external site](https://github.com/dawidseipold/gothic1-crazy-trainer).

### A third-level heading

Third- and fourth-level headings show up indented in the outline on the right.

#### A fourth-level heading

Use these sparingly; most pages only need `##` and `###`.

## Keys and status badges

Inline code with a prefix becomes a component: `key:F1` opens the menu, `key:Ctrl+K` opens search, `key:Shift+F5` is a combination.

Option status flags: `status:OK` `status:BUG` `status:CRASH` `status:TEST` `status:NEW`.

A table of key bindings:

```keys
[
  {"keys": "F1 / Insert", "action": "Open or close the trainer menu"},
  {"keys": "Ctrl+K", "action": "Search the docs"},
  {"keys": "Shift+F5", "action": "Quick save, see [Time and story](doc:time-and-story)"}
]
```

## Callouts

> **Note:** Neutral information, the default kind of remark.

> **Tip:** A shortcut or a good habit.

> **Warning:** Something that can go wrong if you are not careful.

> **Danger:** Something that can break a save or crash the game.

> **Success:** A confirmation that a step worked.
